producer_report.summary: Added the `audience` role and `athena audience`. It fetches the live explainer page (or `--url`/`--reader`). A model reads it as a newcomer and gives a 1–5 rating with findings that each cite evidence. Athena records an `athena.audience-rating/1` record at `records/audience-ratings/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`, and the role definition and invocation record in the same commit. The role is defined in code (`roles::audience`: goal, fixed prompt, cadence 20, path `records/roles/audience-1.json`), so athena.toml, policy.rs and lint config are untouched. Validation refuses ratings outside 1–5 and findings without a source or text. The steward's brief has an "Audience rating" section with the latest rating and findings. `athena status` shows it too, as `audience` in the JSON. A rating of 2 or lower queues a `proposal` work item (role `audience`, key `audience:<rating id>`) that cites the rating's path. Approve or reject it with `athena approve-work` or `athena reject-work`. It does not queue a request on its own, so the audience never starts a change. The explainer URL is one constant, `audience::EXPLAINER_URL`. Docs are in `docs/design/audience-role.md`, `docs/records.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` all pass.

checks_run.note: I ran it with --no-fail-fast -q so every target reported. All pass, including the 7 new tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/audience.rs and the new unit tests. A first run failed the external_calls_guard test; I fixed that (see learnings) and reran.

open_issues: The deliverables list named athena.toml, README.md, docs/architecture.md, athena-cli/src/wiring.rs, and `athena-cli/src/lib.rs`-adjacent files. I left these unchanged on purpose because they were not needed, and the user defaults say to keep the change small. athena.toml and policy.rs are untouched, as criteria 5 and 6 require.

I also changed three files not on the deliverables list: gh.rs (the fetch wrapper), the fake agent in athena-agent/src/fake.rs, and tests/retry.rs. The new `Role::Audience` variant forced the last two, and the guard test forced the first.
The role runs only when asked (`athena audience`). The cadence of 20 finished tasks is recorded in the role definition but nothing schedules it yet. The design doc says so.
The real fetch needs network access and an installed `curl`, and the real model call needs credentials. Only the stubbed path and the fake agent were run here.
I did not mark any requirement row Covered in requirements-map.md and did not touch that file.
mistakes: My first version of audience.rs ran the HTTP client directly and tripped the external-calls guard test. I moved it into gh.rs.
I wrote a schema test that assumed field order and had to make it order-independent.
I used a clippy-flagged `.then().unwrap_or_else()` chain and a very complex tuple return type in a test helper. Both are fixed.
learnings: `crates/athena-core/tests/external_calls_guard.rs` fails any line under crates/ outside gh.rs that runs `gh` or names an HTTP client, including the word `curl` in comments. The page fetch therefore lives in gh.rs as `CurlHttp::get_text`, and `audience::LivePage` delegates to it.

`Role` is a closed enum. Adding `Role::Audience` meant new match arms in the fake agent (athena-agent/src/fake.rs), core's run_pin_tests.rs, and the test script in athena-cli/tests/retry.rs. policy.rs needed no edit.
The schema generator lists `required` properties in alphabetical order, not struct order.
Steward-style runs are not jobs. Their invocation records sit under a job-shaped directory and are loaded into separate lists (`steward_runs`, now also `audience_runs`).
The explainer URL `https://doodla.github.io/athena/` comes from the `repository` field in Cargo.toml plus the Pages setup. No live page was reachable, so I did not check it.
desires: A way to read a long test log without grep or tail. I had to rerun with -q to find the one failing target.
